unclear: REPO holds only modeling_rag.py and retrieval_rag.py; configuration_rag.py and tokenization_rag.py are imported but absent, so defaults of n_docs, max_combined_length, title_sep, doc_sep, do_marginalize, label_smoothing, exclude_bos_score, retrieval_vector_size are not determined by REPO.

Top-level model: three classes exist. RagModel is the shared trunk (question encoder -> retriever -> doc_scores -> generator); RagSequenceForGeneration and RagTokenForGeneration each wrap it as self.rag and add their own marginalization, loss and generate(). Both variants are recorded; they map to the draft's single 'marginalize' and 'nll_loss', split as marginalize_seq / marginalize_token and nll_loss_seq / nll_loss_token.

The code does not fix the encoder/generator architectures: question_encoder is AutoModel.from_config(config.question_encoder) and generator is AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM.from_config(config.generator). The docstring example of from_pretrained_question_encoder_generator pairs a DPR question encoder with t5-small; BART-large (draft) is not stated in REPO. The paper_name 'BART generator' is the draft's.

Grouping differs from the draft: in code the query encoder is RagModel.question_encoder, a sibling of RagRetriever, not part of it; RagRetriever owns the index, passage store, search, passage lookup and the x+z concatenation/tokenization (so those carry parent 'retriever'); the retrieval scores doc_scores are computed in RagModel.forward by torch.bmm, outside the retriever. The RagPreTrainedModel docstring describes 'three components: a question encoder, a dataset retriever and a generator, the encoder and generator are trainable while the retriever is just an indexed dataset'.

The document encoder is not part of the default forward: passage vectors are precomputed in the dataset's 'embeddings' column / the legacy faiss file and only loaded. Which encoder produced them is not in REPO (the legacy index file name 'hf_bert_base.hnswSQ8_correct_phi_128.c_index' hints at a BERT-base encoder). The draft's doc_encoder -> doc_index edge has no counterpart in REPO; RagModel.ctx_encoder exists only for the optional end-to-end training mode.

The search metric is not stated in REPO: HF indexes use dataset.search_batch on whatever faiss index was built; the legacy index is HNSW over vector_size+1 dimensions, with a zero column appended to queries and the last dimension stripped from reconstructed vectors; the code does not explain the extra dimension. 'Maximum Inner Product Search' is the draft's name; the doc_scores used by the model are explicit inner products (bmm).

Concatenation order is passage first: prefix + title + title_sep + text + doc_sep + input string (a TODO comment says the authors would rather put the input first in future models). x reaches it by decoding the question-encoder token ids back to a string and re-tokenizing with the generator tokenizer. The RagModel.forward docstring says input_ids use a generator-compatible tokenizer, but retrieval decodes them with question_encoder_tokenizer; the code path is what is recorded.

question_encoder_last_hidden_state is documented as (batch_size, sequence_length, hidden_size), but it is used as one vector per query (index search input of shape (batch, vector_size), unsqueeze(1) in bmm); the actual shape depends on the question-encoder class, so 'd' is left symbolic.

RAG-Sequence: forward() never marginalizes the logits; the marginalization exists only inside get_nll. The document log-prior is added at target position 1 (second token), not position 0; the code does not say why.
RAG-Sequence 'Fast Decoding' (draft) has no implementation in REPO; generate() implements only 'thorough' decoding (its docstring says so).

Gradient edges are inferred from autograd, not from explicit code: the index-search input is .detach()ed and converted to numpy, and the retrieved index vectors are numpy arrays, so the query encoder gets gradient only through doc_scores = bmm(question_encoder_last_hidden_state, retrieved_doc_embeds^T); the generator gets gradient through its logits. No code in REPO freezes parameters.
text_docs -> doc_index is recorded from CustomHFIndex/CanonicalHFIndex loading a faiss index on the 'embeddings' column; it is a load-time link, not a per-forward computation.

target_y (labels) has no draft component; it is the ground-truth y_j of the draft's loss and the teacher-forcing decoder input during training. output_y carries the draft's paper_name 'target sequence y' for the produced output.
